- Overestimate prices after recent spikes, especially when sentiment is positive or neutral (e.g., +0.3+ sentiment) — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., -1.5+), especially if recent prices are high — model fails to recognize bearish momentum.
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed, model often averages out extremes, leading to lagged corrections — true price moves faster than forecast.
- Mean reversion is overestimated in short-term forecasts — model assumes prices return to mean too quickly, ignoring structural trends.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 3–5 days, model tends to overreact and forecast higher than true outcome — apply downward bias correction.
- If sentiment is consistently negative over 3–5 days, model tends to underreact — apply upward bias correction.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to overconfidence in trend continuation — especially when sentiment is flat or mildly positive — reduce forecast slope.
- When sentiment turns sharply negative after a spike, model often fails to adjust — apply immediate downward correction.
- Avoid extrapolating recent sentiment trends beyond 3–5 days — sentiment can reverse quickly, especially in carbon markets.
